questions.question:
What is the median of the given data?

41, 43, 46, 50, 85, 61, 76, 55, 68, 95
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Arrange the **data** in **ascending order**: 41, 43, 46, 50, 55, 61, 68, 76, 85, 95.

Total number of terms **n = 10** (even).

The **median** is the average of the two middle terms (5th and 6th).

**Median** = (55 + 61) ÷ 2 = 58.

**∴ The correct answer is 58.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 41, 43, 46, 50, 85, 61, 76, 55, 68, 95.

**Formula:** Median = [(n/2)th term + (n/2 + 1)th term] ÷ 2 (when **n** is even).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66c80521e184a8b6c44d64788976507445ca6006ed5a2daf279e2f34171d8f69.png] 

⇒ **Ascending order:** 41, 43, 46, 50, 55, 61, 68, 76, 85, 95.

⇒ Total number of observations (**n**) = 10.

⇒ **Median** = (5th term + 6th term) ÷ 2.

⇒ **Median** = (55 + 61) ÷ 2.

⇒ **Median** = 116 ÷ 2 = 58.

**∴ The correct answer is 58.**

**__Additional Information__**

Median for Odd Observations

If the total number of observations **n** is odd, the **median** is the ((n + 1) ÷ 2)th term after sorting the data.

Mean (Arithmetic Average)

The **mean** is calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations (**n**).

Mode

The **mode** is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A data set can have one mode, more than one mode, or no mode.</p

• **Article 52** of the Constitution of India deals with the office of President.
